selector_column_ecc_dev_hint: Eccentricity scatter across the field — same reading
selector_column_eccentricity_hint: 0 = round, 1 = streak. Weighs twice as much as FWHM in the default weighting
selector_column_fwhm_arcsec_hint: Same quantity in arcseconds — the only one that compares from one instrument to another. Needs the pixel size and the focal length, read from the header or entered by hand
selector_column_fwhm_dev_hint: FWHM scatter **across the field**, not from one frame to the next: it betrays sensor tilt or coma, which a median alone hides
selector_column_fwhm_hint: Full width at half maximum, from an elliptical Gaussian fit on each star (px)
selector_column_psf_hint: Stars actually fitted — a measurement based on three stars is not worth one based on a hundred
selector_column_psfsnr_hint: Signal-to-noise ratio based on PSF photometry (PixInsight formula)
selector_column_psfsw_hint: PSF Signal Weight (PixInsight formula): the signal collected on the stars, weighed against the noise **and** the background. Haze or the Moon raise the background without adding any signal — SNR sees nothing, this one drops
selector_column_rejected_hint: Why the frame is left out of the stack
selector_column_stars_hint: Zero stars is never a good score: it is a measurement that failed
selector_criteria_approval_hint: Python expression; empty = everything is approved. For each measurement: _min, _max, _median, _sigma (deviation from the median in robust dispersion) and _n (min-max).
selector_criteria_min_weight_hint: Fraction of the batch's best score below which the frame is rejected; 0 to reject nothing.
selector_criteria_note: Criteria apply to all groups: an FWHM threshold makes no sense filter by filter. Prefer _sigma to _n to reject — a min-max is flattened by a single bad frame. “Roundness tolerance” is a detection setting: changing it forces a re-measurement, while the other three are re-judged without recomputing anything.
selector_criteria_roundness_hint: A DETECTION parameter: changing it makes the measurements run again on the next run. At the photutils default (1.0), a frame with drifting guiding yields no star at all — and so reads as a perfect frame.
selector_criteria_weighting_hint: Python expression; empty = the WBPP formula. Eccentricity weighs twice as much as FWHM there: a soft frame is still usable, a trailed one will not register.
selector_freeze_title: Locks what the criteria rejected as manual rejections — otherwise changing the expression would silently readmit frames already judged bad
selector_group_not_measured: This group has not been measured yet.
selector_no_measures: No measurements available. Run the pre-processing once: measurements are written to disk and are read back afterwards without recomputing anything.
selector_no_plan: Generate a plan in the Pre-processing tab: that is what carries the measurements.
selector_open_frame_title: Open this frame in the viewport (app.open)
selector_reset_rejects_title: Puts back every frame rejected by hand in this group
selector_table_hint: Enter: open the frame · Space: leave it out or put it back · ◎: reference frame

tour_console_body: This is what sets Retina apart: every click you make writes the equivalent Python line here. Copy it into a script and you have automated the gesture, without learning an API first.
tour_help_body: F1 opens the documentation of whatever process is selected. The command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) reaches everything by name. Enjoy your skies.
tour_pipeline_body: Point this at a folder of raw frames and it plans the whole chain — masters, calibration, registration, integration. The plan is shown before anything runs, and each step can be adjusted.
tour_processes_body: Every operation lives here, grouped by category. Drag one onto an image to apply it, or open its form to set it up — the form is generated from the process itself.
tour_viewport_body: Your images open here. The screen stretch is a display setting: it never touches your pixels, so a linear image can look right without being altered.
tour_welcome_body: A two-minute tour of the five places you will use every day. You can keep clicking around while it runs — nothing is blocked.
